name: Kalser Glocknerstraße
kurzbeschreibung: The Kalser Glocknerstraße leads up to 1,918 m to the Lucknerhaus: the best view of the Großglockner (3,798 m) and gateway to the Nationalpark Hohe Tauern.
oeffnungszeiten: Mitte Mai bis Ende Okt/Nov 24/7 befahrbar (wetterabhängig)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Kalser Glocknerstraße is one of the scenically most awe-inspiring high-alpine roads in Austria and the spectacular gateway to the southern face of the Großglockner massif in Osttirol. Starting from the traditional mountaineering village of Kals am Großglockner at 1,324 metres above sea level, the toll road winds for around seven kilometres through picturesque Ködnitztal up to the alpine inn Lucknerhaus at 1,918 metres above sea level. Nestled within the Nationalpark Hohe Tauern, the terminus of the road offers the most renowned and majestic panorama of the Großglockner (3,798 m), the highest peak in the Republic of Austria.

Landscape & Mountaineering History

The road was inaugurated in 1980 to open up access to upper Ködnitztal and to allow mountaineers as well as excursionists an effortless approach to the monarch of the Hohe Tauern. The route overcomes some 600 metres of elevation gain in gentle switchbacks, leading past thundering glacial streams, flowering alpine pastures, and ancient larch forests. At the Glocknerwinkel car park by the Lucknerhaus, a breathtaking direct view opens onto the formidable southwest face of the Großglockner, the Glocknerwand, and the Ködnitzkees glacier. The area is the historically most prominent starting point for Großglockner ascents via the Stüdlhütte (2,802 m), the Erzherzog-Johann-Hütte (Adlersruhe, 3,454 m), and the normal route. For families and nature lovers, the educational national park theme trail Glocknerspuren – BergeDenken begins here: along a 45-minute circular loop around the Lucknerhaus, information panels and audio stations explain alpine ecology, golden eagles, marmots, and the history of alpine mountaineering pioneers.

Visit & Getting There

The Kalser Glocknerstraße is open daily 24 hours during the summer season from mid-May to late October/November (in deep winter, the roadway serves as a winter hiking path and cross-country ski trail, depending on snow conditions). Toll rates for cars (as of season 2025/2026): short stays up to 3 hours approx. €6.00, up to 6 hours €10.00, day ticket (up to 24 hours) €15.00; multi-day tickets for mountaineers from €18.00 (the toll machine at the barrier exit in Burg accepts cash and debit/credit cards). Motorcyclists pay reduced rates. Arrival by car: from Lienz via the Felbertauernstraße B108 to Huben, turning onto the Kalser Landesstraße L26 into the village centre of Kals am Großglockner, and following the signs into the Ködnitztal (district of Burg). By public transport: VVT bus line 952 from Bahnhof Lienz directly to Kals; during the summer months, the Kalser Glocknerbus shuttle runs regularly up to the Lucknerhaus.

Tips

The grounds around the Lucknerhaus, the viewing platform, and the sun terrace are barrier-free and easily accessible with pushchairs and wheelchairs. Keep an eye out with binoculars for the numerous marmots and chamois on the grassy slopes of the Ködnitztal. Stop in at the Lucknerhaus and savour traditional Osttiroler Schlipfkrapfen ravioli while taking in an unhindered view of the Großglockner.
